requirement:
By default, authoring MUST suppress per-subject `true` judgment lines and show
each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.

`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,
without additional inference. In `--stdout` mode, stdout MUST remain only the
evidence JSON; verbose rationale and other diagnostics MUST go to stderr.
Verbosity MUST NOT change persistence, validation, or exit-status rules.

rationale:
## Judgment: `requirements.authoring.reporting` is satisfied

### Implementation

**Batch (`--all`)**
- `BatchProgress::completed` (`src/authoring/progress.rs`, lines 94–121) counts each judgment for the progress counters.
  - A `true` judgment prints no per-subject line.
  - A `false` judgment prints `<subject>: false (usage: …)`.
  - The recorded Markdown rationale is appended only when `self.verbose` is set.
  - A FIXME judgment prints its notice.
- `BatchProgress::failed` and `println` route authoring errors and false lines through `bar.println` on a terminal, or `eprintln!` when redirected. So output goes to stderr in both modes.
- The progress bar, the counters (true/false/FIXME/errors) and the final `N authored; M unchanged; K failed` summary in `main` are all kept.
- `author_all_with_options` (`src/authoring/batch.rs`) passes `options.verbose` into `BatchProgress`. It reports from the already-completed `AuthoringOutcome`, so no further inference happens.
- Verbosity does not touch the persistence, validation or exit-status logic.

**Single subject** (`main`, `src/main.rs`)
- `-v` is declared as `#[arg(short, long)] verbose`. This is the `-v|--verbose` flag that the invocation requirement specifies.
- A `false` outcome prints `<subject>: false` to stderr. The rationale is printed only under `verbose`.
- `true` outcomes get no judgment line. The metadata line (`subject: backend / model`, plus `— FIXME` when applicable) is kept. So are the `Evidence:` and `Usage:` lines. In file mode these go to stdout. In `--stdout` mode they go to stderr, with `Evidence: stdout`, so stdout holds only the evidence JSON.
- True rationales and input snapshots are never printed.
- Exit status and persistence are unaffected by the flag.

### Tests
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs`
  - `batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose` runs both verbosity settings. In both it checks:
    - no `: true (usage:` line;
    - the false line is present;
    - the FIXME notice and the error are present;
    - no source text and no true rationale appear;
    - the exit status is the same;
    - stdout holds only the summary.
  - It also checks that the rationale appears only when verbose.
  - `terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors` uses a PTY. It checks the counters and summary, that false and FIXME lines appear, that true lines and rationales do not, and that evidence is persisted.
  - `verbose_false_rationale_is_readable_above_terminal_progress` uses a PTY with `-v`. It checks that the rationale is readable alongside the progress display.
  - `failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure` covers visible errors and a nonzero exit status.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs`
  - `false_is_a_completed_assessment` checks that the false line is on stderr, not stdout, and that the rationale is hidden by default.
  - `verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs` covers `-v` and `--verbose` with false, and `-v` with true. It checks that the rationale appears only for false, that no requirement or source text leaks, that `Evidence:` and `Usage:` are retained, and that the evidence is persisted.
  - `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` covers true, false and FIXME, each with and without `--verbose`. It checks that stdout is pure JSON, that diagnostics and metadata go to stderr, that no true line appears, that the rationale appears only for verbose false, and that persistence and usage records are unchanged.

### Remaining observations
- `AuthoringOptions` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`) is marked `{cite}` only, but it is a one-bool plumbing struct. The behaviour lives in code that carries `{impl}`.
- The `(usage: …)` suffix on batch false and FIXME lines is minor extra detail. It is consistent with the usage-record reporting in the authoring requirements.

I found no unacknowledged gaps and no FIXME markers.

each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.
`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,

{cite}`requirements.authoring.invocation` {cite}`requirements.authoring.batch`
:::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]` MUST assess one
existing requirement or named example in the current project. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} batch
`habeas author --all [--config <name>] [-v|--verbose]` MUST author every current requirement
and named example whose evidence is missing, stale, or invalid. It MUST preserve
current records without invoking a model for them, including accepted FIXME
judgments and current false judgments. A current false judgment is reassessed
only when its subject or inputs change, or when it is named explicitly with
{cite}`requirements.authoring.invocation`.
`--all` MUST be mutually exclusive with a subject name and `--stdout`.
Failure to discover declarations or to read, scan, or parse project sources MUST report an error,
not a successful empty batch. A batch with no assessments needed MUST succeed
without resolving model configuration or credentials.
Each subject MUST receive an independent assessment with its own prompt, inputs,
judgment, and usage record. The command MUST report aggregate completion and each
authoring error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.reporting`, and retain
successful writes when another assessment fails. It MUST return a nonzero
exit status if any assessment fails. False judgments MUST still be written as
completed assessments; they remain failures under ordinary evidence validation.
An access-policy denial MUST abort only the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`. Interruption MUST instead stop the
whole batch: queued assessments MUST NOT start, running assessments MUST be
cancelled, and an assessment whose evidence has not been written when the
interruption arrives MUST NOT write it. Evidence already written MUST be
retained, and the command MUST report the number of assessments not started as
a batch failure.
The bundled Habeas skills MUST direct the supervising agent to run this command
to create or refresh evidence. They MUST leave judgments, rationales, and input
snapshots to the authoring harness; the supervising agent addresses findings by
changing requirements, source citations, implementation, or tests.
